transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-30 13:00 PDT
Duration: ~90 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (ParcelDash Product), Rita Morales (ParcelDash ML Platform), Jordan Keane (ParcelDash Eng)
Link to deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/gtm-parceldash-demo-v1 (shared in chat)
---
Summary: Rapid-fire enablement where Redwood SEs run through three customer-specific demo scenarios and practice rebuttals for latency/cost/security objections. Focus on positioning Redwood as the production-first inference partner who can start on hosted then move to Private/Dedicated as volume grows.
Topics covered (auto notes): messaging snippets, fallback story, pilot metrics, demo checklist, competitor differentiation.
---
00:00 Maya: Okay, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, uh, we'll kick off with 10 minutes of framing, then three scenario plays and a live run for the cart-recommendation demo, okay?
00:12 Tom: Yep sounds good, we wanna make sure this resonates with PM and infra teams, especially the latency bits.
00:20 Samir: Great, quick note — we'll call out where to lean on Redwood Optimize for batching and where to call out dedicated pools for predictable throughput.
00:30 Rita: Also we have internal constraints around PII — so the KMS/bring-your-own key story is important.
00:37 Maya: Absolutely, we'll thread in SSO and KMS. Lena will run the failover demo later — hosted fallback to dedicated — show how rollouts and canaries work.
02:05 Lena: Alright scenario one: cart recs at peak — we wanna show 95th percentile latency under 150ms for tail, and cost per 1M tokens estimate. I'll walk through the prompt pattern and the streaming response.
02:24 Jordan: Quick Q — are you demoing the KV cache/prefix caching? Our workload reuses user history a lot.
02:33 Samir: Yes, show caching reduces repeated token costs — we'll demonstrate how prefix caching and automatic KV reuse drop token spend for repeat calls. There's also an example config in the deck.
04:10 Tom: Objection we often hear: why not just use OpenAI managed endpoints — latency seems similar.
04:22 Maya: Good one. High-level: OpenAI is great for fast time-to-market but Redwood differentiates on predictable economics, private deployment options, and operational controls — e.g., per-route token cost breakdowns, canary rollouts, and integrated batching that you tune per workload.
05:05 Rita: And compliance — SOC2 and audit logs?
05:12 Samir: Redwood has SOC2 compliance, audit logs in the console, and integrates with KMS/HSM for customer key management. We'll link the security brief.
07:00 Lena: Now demo flow — walking through the SDK quickstart: create client, select model variant (we'll show a quantized dedicated variant), and then stream responses. Note: the transcript may noise but point out that we can fall back to a cheaper model if throughput spikes.
09:45 Tom: How do you recommend we frame the pricing to finance? They wanna see predictable spend.
09:53 Maya: Pilot recommendation: start hosted with usage caps + unit economics dashboard, run a 4-week pilot with SLOs (latency, accuracy), then commit to dedicated if 99th percentile latency or throughput hits thresholds in week 3. We'll provide an estimated commit chart.
11:30 Samir: Quick technical aside — if ParcelDash needs strict region residency, Redwood Private can run in your VPC or on-prem and still keep the same API surface. That's a key sell to regulated customers.
13:55 Lena: Scenario two: invoice parsing / routing where accuracy regression is unacceptable. We'll demo the eval harness—how you pin prompt sets and run regression tests across model changes.
15:16 Rita: We need the eval examples to include our edge case addresses and tracking IDs — can you include a small labeled set?
15:25 Maya: Yes we'll ask for a 100-example seed set. Samir will map those to the eval harness.
17:40 Samir: Demo note — when doing long-form outputs it's better to use structured output support and function calling so you reduce hallucination and make parsing deterministic. We'll show an example of model -> structured JSON output with post-processing.
20:05 Tom: Competitor angle — what if they say Anthropic has a safety-first narrative?
20:20 Maya: Acknowledge safety but pivot: Redwood's strength is operational controls + the ability to run in Private with customer keys and integrate with your infra. You can use Anthropic models in parallel, but Redwood gives the serving ergonomics and rollout controls to operate at scale.
22:30 Lena: Ok live run — Cart recommendation demo (scenario 3). I'll start the demo app. Heads up this is a mock dataset to avoid PII.
22:50 (brief pause, background typing)
23:12 Lena: Showing the prompt template now — we include user context, last 5 interactions, and product embeddings. Streaming on — you can see tokens arriving in the UI.
24:08 Jordan: That streaming looks smooth — what's the client timeout default?
24:15 Samir: Default SDK timeout is 30s but we recommend per-route overrides. For streaming we usually set a 60s longer tail for larger responses.
26:30 Tom: Is the KV cache shared across instances or per-tenant?
26:38 Samir: It's per-customer namespace by default, but you can configure shared caches in dedicated deployments if you want cross-tenant reuse (rare for compliance).
28:55 Lena: Now I'm going to simulate a capacity spike and trigger the fallback path — hosted calls should route to a compatible cheaper model or dedicated pool depending on policy. Watch the route and the canary traffic.
29:08 (sound of multiple window clicks)
29:32 Lena: Okay fallback engaged — you can see a slight latency bump but the app stays live. This is the kind of graceful degradation we emphasize.
31:10 Tom: Nice — how much engineering effort to switch from hosted to private once we decide to commit?
31:18 Maya: For Private we do a planning week for VPC peering, KMS integration, and a smoke-test plan. Work is usually 3–6 weeks depending on infra SLAs. Dedicated is faster — usually 1–2 weeks to provision GPU pools after contract.
33:00 Rita: Security follow-up — we need an architecture diagram and the SOC2 certs, plus a list of encryption-at-rest details.
33:10 Samir: We'll attach the security whitepaper and certs after the call. Also, provide a link to the runtime network diagram.
34:22 Tom: Pricing question again — what about tokenization differences across models affecting cost estimates?
34:30 Samir: Good point — we'll include a tokenization appendix and an adjusted estimate for your payload mix in the one-pager.
36:00 Maya: Quick roleplay — Rita will play procurement, Tom you'll be PM. We'll practice the 60-second pitch and then run objections.
36:15 Rita (as procurement): "We are concerned about vendor lock-in and exit strategy."
36:25 Maya: "Fair — we support standard model formats, exportable logs, and a defined offboarding plan that includes model artifacts and cached prefixes. Cost-wise we also recommend a staged migration plan to ease the transition."
38:42 Jordan: Can you show the A/B rollout for a model change?
38:51 Lena: Yep, here's the canary UI — set 10% traffic to new variant, monitor quality metrics from evals, then promote. If a regression shows up the automatic fallback reverts to stable.
41:00 Tom: That helps. For the pilot, what's a recommended success criteria set?
41:08 Maya: Proposal: uptime >99.5 (service), p95 latency <200ms for recs, accuracy delta <1% vs baseline, and cost per active user under $X — we'll customize that number based on your dataset.
43:12 Samir: Demo technical notes — when you run benchmarks we'll provide both token-level and infra-level metrics so you can see server-side GPU utilization. That helps finance and SREs.
45:30 Lena: Final live run — full flow from request to response to logging. Note some transcribe artifacts may show in captions but the console logs are accurate.
47:00 (short hiccup, someone drops audio for ~10s)
47:20 Maya: Minor audio glitch, okay continuing.
49:10 Tom: Overall this was useful, two asks — send security pack and a sample benchmark script.
49:22 Maya: We'll do that. Also propose we run a 4-week pilot starting with hosted and a capped budget.
50:00 Rita: Sounds reasonable.
52:30 Maya: Recap of next steps — Samir will share benchmark script, Maya will send one-pager and pricing band, Lena will run a scripted failover demo in next call. Proposed pilot kickoff 2025-08-11.
52:55 Jordan: Can we get a sample SLO dashboard screenshot to show execs?
53:10 Samir: I'll include SLO dashboard screenshots in the follow-up email.
54:00 Maya: Ok thanks everyone. End.
---
Post-call notes: attendees rated session as practical and actionable in chat. Action items captured above. Additional artifacts to attach: security_whitepaper.pdf, pilot_pricing_estimate.xlsx, benchmark_script_instructions.md.
